basics.description: **Botkins on Azure.** This makes one VM that runs Botkins with its own relay. When the deployment finishes, open **Outputs** and open **pairingLink** on your phone to pair the Botkins app. You need nothing else: no SSH key, and no files to download. This works from a phone.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Where the VM runs. If a VM size isn't available here, pick another region.

basics.name: vmName
basics.label: VM name
basics.toolTip: Also the start of the server's web address.

constraints.validationMessage: 2 to 40 letters, numbers and hyphens, starting with a letter.

basics.name: screenAccess
basics.label: Screen access
basics.toolTip: Adds a virtual screen with Google Chrome. Your phone can see it and control it, for example to finish a sign-in page that a bot opened. You can change this later with `botkins-server screen on` or `off`.

options.text: After you pair, turn the screen on from the phone in **Settings › Screen**. It starts at **Off**. Before the phone allows **View only** or **View and control**, it asks for Face ID or your passcode.

basics.name: vmSize
basics.label: VM size
basics.toolTip: 2 vCPUs and 4 GB is enough, with or without Screen access.

options.text: Both are optional. You can also sign in after you pair: in the Botkins app, open **Settings › Models**. The tokens go to the VM in encrypted settings, and Botkins keeps them sealed in its vault.

elements.name: claudeCodeToken
elements.toolTip: On a computer that is signed in to your Claude plan, run `claude setup-token` and paste the token here.

elements.name: githubCopilotToken
elements.toolTip: A GitHub token for an account that has Copilot, for example from `gh auth token`.

elements.name: pushNotifications
elements.label: Send iPhone notifications through relay.botkins.app
elements.toolTip: Each notification is sealed for your phone. The Botkins relay only passes it to Apple. Clear this to send no notifications. Then nothing leaves your server for Botkins.

elements.name: certificateEmail
elements.label: Certificate email (optional)
elements.toolTip: Gets only notices about the HTTPS certificate. It also lets the server use ZeroSSL if Let's Encrypt is busy.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter an email address, or leave it empty.

elements.name: allowSsh
elements.label: Allow SSH (optional)
elements.toolTip: Most people don't need SSH. The phone app does the daily work, and Azure Run Command runs `botkins-server` commands from the portal or the Azure CLI.

elements.name: sshPublicKey
elements.label: SSH public key
elements.toolTip: Paste a public key, such as the contents of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub. To make one, run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` on your computer.

constraints.validationMessage: Paste one public key. It starts with ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa or ecdsa-sha2-.

elements.name: sshAllowedFrom
elements.label: Allow SSH from
elements.toolTip: The IP address or CIDR range that may connect to SSH, for example your home's public IP. SSH stays closed to everyone else.

constraints.validationMessage: An IPv4 address or CIDR range.

elements.name: adminUsername
elements.label: SSH user name
elements.toolTip: Any name except botkins, which is the account the Botkins service runs as.
